correctness.rationale: Direct Fourier multiplication, explicit root propagation and absorbing-zero product give the exact magma isomorphism. The finite maximal-subquandle proof uses surjectivity of right multiplication and support intersections; odd local orders prove connected Latin fibers. The ideal argument constructs for every smaller support target a right multiplier via unique square roots, and proves the converse by support intersection. Group-one and empty-ideal boundaries are specified. Direct finite-field multiplication checks (29,974 comparisons) and exhaustive ideal subsets for three base cases independently passed.

originality.rationale: The evaluated prior 2026 orbit-count theorem covers all complex idempotents and their Peirce multiplicities, but not the induced magma, maximal quandle strata, or exact two-sided ideal lattice. The proof derives the multiplication law and proves the surjectivity and ideal-reachability implications, yielding a qualitatively different classification. The earlier 2022 idempotent-quandle theorem assumes integral coverings, not all finite odd-order complex cores. The risk of an equivalent existing semilattice-of-quandles formulation remains material.

value.rationale: Idempotent-generated quandles are a motivated object in the 2022 covering-quandle literature. This complete all-odd-complex-core classification distinguishes the entire idempotent magma from its maximal connected Latin quandle components, identifies the canonical embedded core, and determines all two-sided subset ideals via Boolean down-sets and their exact Dedekind-number count. These are intrinsic structural invariants, not a minor recomputation of the previously known number of idempotents.
